title: Selection & iteration
examples: When should I use an if statement instead of a loop?
What is the difference between a for loop and a while loop?
How do I count the number of times a loop runs?

explain.say: Today we look at making decisions in code. We use if statements for this.
An if statement checks if a condition is true. If it is true, the code inside runs. Otherwise, it skips it.
We can use else statements too. The else part runs only if the if condition was false.
For loops repeat code a set number of times. You tell it exactly how many times to run.
While loops repeat code as long as a condition stays true. You must check the condition first.
Nested loops mean putting one loop inside another loop. This repeats actions in a grid pattern.

draw.text: Outer loop controls rows, inner loop controls columns

faq.q: How do I know when to use a for loop versus a while loop?
faq.a: Use a for loop when you know the exact number of times you need to repeat something. Use a while loop when you need to repeat until something changes.
asks: Should I use for or while?
When is a loop count fixed?

faq.q: What happens if I forget to change the variable in a while loop?
faq.a: The condition will always be true, causing an infinite loop. This will make your program run forever until you stop it.
asks: How do I stop a while loop?

faq.q: Can I use if statements inside loops?
faq.a: Yes, you can. You can check a condition on every single pass through a loop. This makes the code very flexible.
asks: Can I check something inside a for loop?

faq.q: What is the purpose of nested loops?
faq.a: They are used when you need to process data in two dimensions, like rows and columns on a spreadsheet. Think of drawing a grid.
asks: When do I need two loops?

faq.q: Do I need to set up variables before using loops?
faq.a: Yes, if you are counting or checking a condition, you must initialize the variable first. Otherwise, the loop might start with an unknown value.
asks: Do I start the counter variable?

facts: An if statement executes code only if its condition evaluates to true.
A for loop is best when the number of repetitions is predetermined.
A while loop continues executing as long as its specified condition remains true.
Nested loops are used to process data that has both row and column dimensions.

quiz.say: If you want to print the numbers one through ten, which structure is best?
quiz.why: The for loop is designed for counting a fixed number of times.

wrong.1: This requires manually setting i to 0 and incrementing it inside, which is more work.
wrong.2: An if statement only runs once, it does not repeat the action.
wrong.3: This is not valid programming syntax for controlling repetition.

quiz.say: A program needs to keep asking the user for input until they type the word 'quit'. Which loop should be used?
quiz.why: The while loop checks a condition repeatedly until that condition becomes false.

wrong.0: This is not standard programming syntax for flow control.
wrong.2: This loop would run exactly ten times, regardless of the user's input.
wrong.3: An if statement only checks the condition once and then stops.

quiz.say: To print every coordinate pair (x, y) in a 3 by 4 grid, what structure must you use?
quiz.show: Outer loop for rows, Inner loop for columns

options.show: Outer loop for rows, Inner loop for columns
options.say: Outer loop for rows, Inner loop for columns

quiz.why: Nested loops are required to control two different sets of repeating actions, like rows and columns.

wrong.0: A single loop cannot manage two independent sets of repeating counts simultaneously.
wrong.1: If statements only check conditions; they do not guarantee repeating actions.
wrong.3: Separate loops would run the actions one after the other, not in a grid pattern.
